comments.author: Sophia
comments.body: Chain quests like these cannot be repeated, unless you lose the discovery card related to them. FSD cannot be made into an ornament, but with Treasure Hunting, you have the option to use a discovery card when combining clues -- if FSD appears, and if you lose the card, then you can repeat it. I did this with King Muryeong's Tomb (Songsunri). The cards you can use appear to be randomly selected, though, so it may take a while.

comments.author: Will_Adams
comments.body: If any character you're fleeted to(whether to meet any of the quest requirements or not) has completed this quest, it will not show for you. The same goes for any quest that can't be pulled more than one time. And yes, quests, especially harder to pull ones, show much easier if your character trying to pull them meets all of the requirements, even languages. ie: the quest from the Stockholm merchant mediator "Procure food for soldiers" that gets you the Chef job card will show much easier if your character(or one of their aides) speaks Nordic as well as having Cooking r5 and 5k trade fame.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
It is true that quests that are part of a larger chain, like this one, do not typically reappear for people who have discovered them, but I've had several fleetmates successfully pull quests like these despite being in fleet with me after I've found them, and vice versa (and before the steps mentioned further down this comment). Being fleeted with others really has no effect on whether or not a quest will appear for you personally; you can leech skills while on a quest, but not in pulling it.

Additionally, if you can lose the discovery card for a quest like this one (discussed in the comments section of A culture without water ) then you can pull the quest again at any time; completing the quest again will regain the lost discovery card, thus making the quest impossible to pull until you've lost the card again.

I personally have made it a point to lose certain cards for quests like Fort San Domingo and Leshan Giant Buddha, so that I can re-pull them for others if need be. And yes, meeting quest requirements does appear to make even the rare ones more likely to spawn as long as fame requirements (and sometimes port permits) are met. There are some job quests like Tailor and Sommelier which have shown up without any skill requirements being met lately, though.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
1. Have the listed fame.
2. Have East Asia port permits.
3. Have the listed skills (boost equips are okay), or fleet with someone who does, to be able to discover/complete quest. Note that I have seen this quest appear even without the required skills, but...
4. Chinese language (sold in Macau, or available as translation notes/dictionaries from Industrial Revolution towns) might help raise likelihood of the quest appearing. It's not necessary for quest steps as no archive reading is required, but it does seem like quests show up more frequently with the required language.

Otherwise, there are apparently no other requirements. You can take the quest without even having discovered Tamsui.

comments.author: Gudebuddha
comments.body: Your alts having skills does not change anything for getting quests. Most (maybe even all) quest you can get without having all needed skills and the quest checks if YOU (including your aides) have the needed skills, your alts skills do not matter at that point. You might be able to spawn the quest without having recognition 10, but it might be very hard to do, maybe even close to impossible, i have not tried. If you try: get as many of the skills as possible (incuding the lang.) and give it a go, no guarantee though. Getting Archeo 12 and Recog 10 on the same toon might be easier, or leech the quest from someone who has that.
